content:
marta: Quick heads-up — AcmeCorp POC hit a blocker. They're testing streaming with function/tool calls + structured JSON output. We need: (1) short guide for SDK handshake across proxy, (2) ephemeral creds pattern for their security team, and (3) pricing estimate for expected qps. Can someone own?

sam: I can sketch the SDK steps. do they want SSE or websocket?

marta: They prefer websocket for bidirectional events. primary ask: deterministic schema for tool responses so they can validate downstream.

jess: For websocket + function calls, share this snippet they can run quickly:```js// init
const client = new RedwoodWS({ token: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.open();
await client.callFunction('invoice_parser', { pdf: base64 });
```Works with our node SDK (v0.9.x).

kevin: Security note: Acme's infosec requires ephemeral creds (rotating for every session), audit logs, and KMS integration for any customer data we persist. We should propose STS-like short-lived tokens + audit webhook.

olivia: I can draft the security appendix. quick Q: do they need on-prem or VPC? that affects the KMS workflow.

marta: VPC-only. they said on-site key management and SOC2 requirements.

sam: Ok — handshake over VPC proxy: use mutual TLS for socket upgrade. Example curl for handshake:```bash
curl -X POST https://proxy.acme/v1/handshake \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>" \
  -d '{"proto":"websocket","want_functions":true}'
```Server returns a session token + suggested model variant.

jess: Also call out structured output schema. Suggest `tool_response` envelope:```json
{"tool": "invoice_parser", "status": "ok", "result": {"total": 123.45, "currency": "USD"}}
```Adds deterministic keys so their validators can assert types.

kevin: For compliance: include retention TTLs in the appendix. default 30 days for logs, ephemeral payloads never persisted unless customer opts in. Add KMS wrap for any stored artifacts.

marta: Pricing: they expect ~150 rps sustained, bursts to 700 for batch ingestion windows. can we get back with per-token + reserved capacity options?

olivia: Quick calc — assuming avg 200 tokens per request. hosted per-token is $0.0008/token => rough hosted cost = 150 rps * 200 * 3600 * 24 * 30 * 0.0008 = big number. I'll get a cleaner sheet. But we should give them two options: hosted (pay-as-you-go) and Dedicated (monthly commit + discounted rate).

sam: If we recommend Dedicated, note that batching & prefix caching can reduce token consumption by ~35% for their flow. include sample config:```yaml
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_latency_ms: 25
cache:
  prefix_kv: true
```

jess: Also flag streaming limits: websocket concurrency per connection is 10 active tool calls; recommend multiplexing across connections for parallelism.

marta: Action items: 1) sam — SDK handshake guide + example repo (ETA EOD), 2) olivia — security appendix + KMS runbook (ETA tomorrow), 3) kevin — retention & compliance bullets (ETA tomorrow), 4) jess — sample schema + client example (ETA EOD), 5) i'll own pricing note with hosted vs Dedicated numbers (ETA EOD).

kevin: +1 on timeline. I'll also attach the standard security questionnaire template to the thread when ready.

deploy-bot: deploy status: sample repo 'acme-poc-ws' created at https://git.redwood/integrations/acme-poc-ws (private). :rocket:

olivia: one more thought — ask Acme if they can accept structured return codes for partial failures (e.g., invoice page parse errors). saves retries.

marta: good call. i'll surface that in the next call. thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: ping if anyone wants to pair on the sample repo later.

jess: dropping a mini-runbook in the repo: README -> quickstart -> structured_schema.md

marta: last note: make sure the SDK example includes `function_call` semantics and explicit content-type `application/json+tool` so their proxies don't mangle payloads.

kevin: noted. attaching a short snippet for token rotation pattern to the repo in a minute.
